messages:
maria: FYI I'm opening a small infra PR to move svc `edge-web` from NodePort->LoadBalancer (NLB) so we can attach customer edge certs. PR: https://git.redwood.dev/r/infra/edge/+/1234

kevin: quick q — do we want TLS termination at the LB or passthrough to pod? If terminate at LB we lose host routing unless we front with ALB

maria: current plan is NLB with TLS listeners + target port 8443 to envoy ingress (so TLS passthrough at LB, terminate in envoy). Reason: we need client certs and mTLS later, and want static IPs

ashley: +1 for passthrough. For healthchecks make sure service has `healthPort` set and `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` so source IP preserved. Also NLB healthchecks are on instance port by default, so our nodePort needs to be open.

jordan: note that terraform change will create aws_lb_target_group with target_type = "ip" if using IP mode. If using node ports it will be instance. here's snippet:

``
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "edge" {
  port     = 8443
  protocol = "TCP"
  target_type = "ip"
  health_check {
    protocol = "TCP"
    port     = "8443"
  }
}
```

kevin: if we go ip targets we need to update k8s service annotations: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: ip` and also `aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: TCP`

maria: good catch. Also how do we wire certs? options: attach ACM cert to NLB TLS listener (if terminating) or use cert-manager to provision certs into k8s secret and let envoy handle TLS. I prefer envoy + cert-manager for wildcard certs under our DNS and automation.

ashley: agree. cert-manager with `aws-route53` DNS challenge or `aws-privateca` works. Make sure secret name matches envoy ingress config. We'll also need a `kubectl patch secret` step in rollout plan if we rotate.

maria: PR updated with cert-manager manifests + service annotations. PTAL @kevin @ashley @jordan

deploy-bot: CI passed for infra/terraform (plan: no-destroy). plan url: https://ci.redwood.dev/blue/infra/1234/plan

kevin: quick code review comments: a) add `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` b) add annotation `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: nlb-ip` c) add tf outputs for LB DNS cname and target group arn

jordan: for canary: we can create a canary service with selector `canary: true` and register it to a separate target group, then use Route53 weighted records to shift traffic 10%->90% while we monitor latency and 5xxs.

maria: sweet. I'll push updates and request a review. expected rollout: small canary tonight, full switch tomorrow morning PST. If anyone has objections speak now.

ashley: no objections. :thumbsup:

kevin: sounds good, ping me when ready to merge

maria: thanks all!
